$comment: Mirror-pairing schema for All That Glitters. User-maintained; edit to correct pairings for new map versions. See mirror_by_start_position.mjs for how this is consumed.

splitAxis.description: ATG has two structural mirror types. The 2 back-centre slots per side (those near the map's horizontal midline) are 180° point-reflected opposites: flip BOTH x and z through the map centre. The remaining 6 flank slots per side are single-axis (Z-only) mirror opposites: keep the same horizontal side, flip only z. Left-flank bottom pairs with left-flank top; right-flank bottom pairs with right-flank top.

backMiddle.note: Positions where abs(x - mapW/2) < xRangeFromCenter are classified as back-middle and use full point-reflection (XZ). For ATG at mapW=6144 this means 2072 < x < 4072.

flank.note: All other positions use Z-only reflection. 'matchSameSide' restricts candidates to the same horizontal half of the map (x < mapW/2 matches x < mapW/2, etc.), so left-flank pairs with left-flank and right-flank pairs with right-flank. When one side has more flank players than the other (players chose asymmetric spawns), the excess are left unpaired.

knownSlots.$comment: Approximate canonical spawn positions observed on ATG v2.2.3. Coordinates in elmos. Role and position number added for named positions (see positionRoles below). Used for documentation; the algorithm classifies by actual commander-spawn position, not these values.

techSpawnMexes.$comment: Metal extractor positions for the Tech player spawn (position 6). Coordinates in elmos, ±8 elmos accuracy (metal map is 16 elmos/pixel). Extracted from ATG2.smf binary inside all_that_glitters_v2.2.3.sd7. 7th mex = most likely meta pick; confirm from current BAR community consensus.

seventh_mex.note: back-right corner — safe expansion, most likely new meta 7th pick; confirm from current BAR community
top-right corner — safe expansion, most likely new meta 7th pick; confirm from current BAR community

positionRoles.$comment: Named position roles for ATG. Orientation: your team at bottom (high Z), opponents at top (low Z). 4 front positions (low-Z end of your half) numbered left-to-right (1-4), back positions numbered 5-8 (not strictly left-to-right: 5=far-left, 7=left-center, 6=center-right, 8=far-right). Front positions have an F-number abbreviation (F1-F4). Laning is cross-mirror: the map flips, so F1 lanes against enemy F4, F2 against F3, F3 against F2, F4 against F1.

roles.description: Far-left front. Fights into the canyon from the open side. Named for strategic opposition to the canyon geography on the right side of the map.
roles.notes: Metal-rich side; creates a mismatch advantage vs the opposing Canyon position.

roles.description: Center front. Faces opponents pushing from multiple directions — expects to fight 'a rainbow of enemy colors'.

Far-right front, inside the canyon geography. Fewer mexes than other positions; generally does not contest mexes outside the canyon. Economically weaker, creating a metal mismatch vs the opposing AC position.
roles.notes: Metal deficit vs AC makes even-unit-count fights unfavorable; relies on canyon geography for defensive advantage.

roles.description: Far-left back, directly behind the AC position. Starts with 6 mexes; picks up 1-2 front mexes when AC is winning the front.
Center-right back. Bypasses early unit production to build the T2 factory, funnels team resources into a single T2 factory, then produces multiple T2 constructors to distribute across the team.
roles.notes: Acts as team T2 hub; individual economy sacrificed early for team-wide T2 acceleration.

roles.description: Left-center back. Opens with an air factory (Cortex faction preferred — Shuriken interceptors are strong early), transitioning into air-based harassment and control.
Far-right back, behind the Canyon position. Canyon-side mirror of Back Corner. Starts with 6 mexes; picks up 1-2 front mexes when the enemy allows it.
roles.notes: Symmetric to Back Corner (pos 5) in structure but on the canyon flank; canyon geography may constrain front mex access more than the AC-side equivalent.
